result:
Solution 1 gives the answer I believe is correct, though I am relying on a recalled result and a classical analogy rather than a full derivation.

A Hecke eigensystem λ of finite ℘-slope has a nonzero U_℘-eigenvalue. In the classical setting, oldforms at level Np^r coming from a form f of level Np are spanned by f(z), f(pz), …, f(p^{r-1}z). On this span, U_p has the single nonzero eigenvalue α, with the other eigenvalues equal to 0. So an eigensystem with nonzero U_p-eigenvalue occurs with multiplicity 1, not r.

The Drinfeld analogue, which I recall from the literature, says the finite-slope part is unchanged when the ℘-power in the level increases. That makes the ratio 1.

The other two solutions do not hold up:
- Solution 2 claims the multiplicity is multiplied by r. That counts all oldforms, including those on which U_℘ acts as 0, so it does not apply to finite slope.
- Solution 3 claims a factor q^{2D(r-1)}. The solution itself is openly unsure ("Hmm... I'll go with"), and it has no solid justification.

Solution 1's justification is loose: it says the α-eigenspace is one-dimensional for all r, and calls it a "newform vector," which is not quite the right language. Its conclusion, 1, still matches the expected result.

CHOICE: 1
